title: Dot — the living footnote
oneLiner: A small expressive dot carries a question to the exact on-page words or link that answer it, then anchors your local note there.
targetFeeling: A little reader shares your attention; you see exactly where its answer comes from.
gesture: Drag Dot onto a paragraph, menu section, or captioned photo; ask one short question; follow its landing; select text to pin a note.
magicMoment: Dot leaves the terrace photo, rolls to the policy sentence, and replies beside the highlighted words; missing evidence brings it home.
example: Drop Dot onto the restaurant terrace photo and ask: Smoking allowed? The caption sets context.
Dot lands beside Smoking permitted only in the designated terrace area and preserves the qualification.
On the unstated-policy variant, Dot returns to the photo: Page does not say. An outdoor photo is not permission.
must: Toolbar-invoked unpacked MV3 extension with activeTab, scripting and storage; three localhost reference pages: /permitted.html, /prohibited.html, /unstated.html; reject unsupported pages.
Expressive 28-pixel draggable body; highlighted paragraph/menu/photo target; caption or alt text for photos; one question up to 160 characters; smoking and Book intents.
Scroll and travel to exact highlighted source text; adjacent reply up to 30 words preserving qualifications; distinguish absent evidence, unsupported question, and extraction failure.

One real constrained model call if credentials are ready: Ask previews explicitly selected context and local evidence, at most 1,200 characters; validate returned evidence ID and verbatim quote, then render a reviewed reply preserving qualifications; fixed code controls actions.
One editable local text-anchored note; URL, exact quote, and surrounding text stored locally; reload restore and scroll/resize positioning; missing anchor shows Original text changed.
Point to original Book anchor and destination; only the user's click opens /booking-info.html, the fictional booking-information landing page; no booking form interaction.
nonGoals: Universal sites, Gmail, PDFs, iframes, hidden content, image understanding, and dynamic-page anchor repair.
Chat history, multiple pets, proactive advice, general browsing, and cross-page research.
Completed bookings, form filling, messages, accounts, note sync, and publishing.

demo.action: Invoke Dot on the fictional restaurant; drag it for a squishy landing.
Drop on the terrace photo; ask Smoking allowed?; submit bounded evidence preview.
Follow Dot to the exact permission sentence and designated-area condition.
Repeat on the unstated variant; Dot returns with Page does not say.
Select text, pin Ask about terrace seating, and scroll to show attachment.
Ask Where can I book?; follow Dot to the original Book link; click and stop at booking information.

risk: Stable source extraction, precise text anchoring, and legible travel across page layouts are harder than giving Dot personality; static fixtures do not establish arbitrary-site competence.
fallback: Reviewed smoking/Book intents resolve deterministically to checked DOM quotes or reviewed page absence. Label Local evidence. Unsupported questions abstain; failed extraction or quote mismatch never means page does not say. Cut model integration after 45 minutes without a reliable round trip.
verdict: Recommend the living-footnote version: every answer has a landing place; missing evidence brings Dot home. Spend the five hours on pointing, evidence travel, one local pin, and the original Book link.

sources.title: Chrome Extensions — activeTab
sources.takeaway: Observed documentation: explicit invocation grants temporary current-tab access; scripting allows injection; same-origin navigation can retain access. Design inference: enforce a separate three-page support boundary.

sources.title: Chrome Extensions — Content scripts
sources.takeaway: Observed documentation: content scripts access page DOM from isolated JavaScript execution. Design inference: a resident overlay is plausible, but layout compatibility remains unproven.

sources.title: W3C CSSOM View — Range.getClientRects
sources.takeaway: Observed specification: selected text has rectangles; returned geometry is not live. Design inference: exact landings and pins need recomputation after scroll or resize.
